title: Count the FLOPs
hints: Count first: an (M, K) @ (K, N) matmul does M * N * K multiply-adds, and each one is 2 FLOPs.

The formula is right; the arithmetic isn't. `2 * 2048 * 2048 * 2048` is 2^34, and `int` keeps only the low 32 bits, all zeros, so you'll probably see 0. It's signed overflow, so the compiler is allowed to do anything at all.
`2 * M * N * K` is computed in `int` before it becomes `long long`. Make the first factor a `long long` so every multiply happens in 64 bits.
explain: The reference writes `2LL * M * N * K`. Starting with a `long long` literal makes every multiplication 64-bit, so 2048^3 * 2 never overflows the 32-bit `int` along the way.
